text:
emily: opened a docs PR for the model catalog change + migration guide. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/958 - includes a short changelog blurb and a migration subsection for SDK users.
ravi: nice. can you include both a Python SDK snippet and a curl example for our quickstart users? PM asked for a minimal copy-paste.
emily: adding both. python snippet will show the param rename and a note about SDK >= 2.1 required. curl example will be a one-liner.
jordan: changelog needs a clear deprecation timeline and the recommended fallback model. include exact dates (deprecate on 2026-05-15, removal 2026-06-15) and a sentence about model performance differences.
emily: noted. I'll add the dates and a small note comparing latency/cost numbers (approx).
maria: quick heads-up about preview: big model tables have been flaking out in preview; prefer splitting the table into smaller per-category pages or use a collapsed accordion. preview-bot frequently times out on > 200 rows.
emily: ok i'll split by family and move the giant JSON example into snippets/model-mapping.json to reduce page weight.
alex: for reviewers, can we tag @ravi, @jordan, and @alex? i'll take tone / release blurb. also adding @ops-release for merge coordination.
ravi: I'll review for accuracy and the SDK example. small suggestion: show the SDK error users will see if they use old param name, e.g. "400 Bad Request: unknown parameter 'response_mode'".
jordan: also add a migration note for self-hosted customers: they need to update their config manifest to use the new model id, and include a sample sed command to bulk-update manifests.
emily: adding sed example.

# examples to include in PR body (inline):

python snippet:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$RW_KEY")
# old usage
resp = client.generate(model="model-legacy-y", response_mode="fast")
# new usage
resp = client.generate(model="model-new-y", response_style="fast")
```

curl one-liner:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -d '{"model":"model-new-y","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sed bulk update (self-hosted):
```bash
find ./manifests -name '*.yaml' -exec sed -i 's/model-legacy-y/model-new-y/g' {} +
```

maria: preview-bot queued a build when you pushed the snippets.

alex: looks clean. smaller tables render fine. marketing wants a very short changelog sentence for public release notes; i've drafted one in the PR description. jordan please sanity-check tone.
jordan: draft is fine. consider adding the exact ticket number for cross-reference.
emily: done. question about merge order: ops-release suggests flip infra default first, then merge docs. i'd prefer merging docs first so public docs and migration steps exist before we flip traffic to the new model. what do others think?
ravi: both approaches have tradeoffs. merging docs first prevents 404s and lets us link from release announcement immediately. merging after infra flip prevents early discovery of the new model before it's available. ops should coordinate a locked window.
maria: ops prefers: create a short maintenance window, merge docs into a locked branch, then ops flips infra, then we merge to main. this avoids brief mismatches. propose the checklist in PR: 
- tag release manager (@ops-release)
- push docs branch to main-proposed (w/ draft blurb)
- ops flip model default during window
- merge PR after flip confirmed
- publish release notes
emily: adding that checklist to PR description. also added a CHANGELOG entry in releases repo (link).
alex: reviewers assigned: ravi, jordan, alex. can we get approvals by end of day Monday? release window Tuesday morning.
ravi: I can review by EOD.
jordan: will review Monday AM.
preview-bot: PR #958 merged by emily at 1843004911
emily: merged after ops confirmed flip at 1843004500. closing loop and will notify marketing for the announcement. :rocket:
